newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 13.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Consumer prices increased this April by only 0.6 percent. Despite this, there was an increase in prices for postal and telecommunication services by 15.2 percent. Without this influence, monthly inflation would have been just above 0.4 percent. The yearly inflation rate after the first third of this year was 8.2 percent (year-on-year 6.7 percent), and analysts agree that it will decline during the next quarter.

- AR Stavebni Sporitelna had net profits in 1996 of 115 million crowns. According to its general director Vaclav Soukup, the profits were divided into two parts, one for covering basic expenses and the other for strengthening reserves.
- President Vaclav Havel will fly to the United States today with his wife Dagmar Havlova. During the visit, Havel and German President Roman Herzog will receive an award for European statesmen.
- Shareholders of Tamda Usti nad Labem, a pharmaceutical distributor, decided to merge with Respharma and Moraviapharm. The majority shareholder of all three companies is Chemapol Group.

LIDOVE NOVINY - The Czech Republic addressed the EU with a note in which it announced that it will not cancel its import deposit system. After May 19, the EU will receive more detailed material to show that restricting imports is not in violation of their agreement.

- Labour unions did not manage in yesterday's meeting of the board of the Council for Dialogue of Social Partners to get the cabinet to return to the question of deregulation of rents and energy prices.
- This week or next, the cabinet should discuss a proposal to increase pensions on average by about 10 percent from August 1, according to Labour and Social Affairs Minister Jindrich Vodicka.
- After meeting with President Vaclav Havel yesterday, the chairman of the Civic Democratic Alliance, Michael Zantovsky, said restructuring of the cabinet is a matter of a few months.
- Skoda Tezke Strojirenstvi, a subsidiary of Skoda Plzen, signed a contract worth $46 million to build two factories for processing sugar cane in Khuzestan, Iran.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Coalition Chairmen Vaclav Klaus (ODS), Michael Zantovsky (ODA) and Josef Lux (KDU-CSL) agreed yesterday that they will have a large coalition meeting after the parliament meeting in May. The main theme will be administrative organisation.
- The new Regional Development Minister Tomas Kvapil, who was sworn in yesterday by President Vaclav Havel, could become a strength for the cabinet, according to the president.
- The unemployment rate, which has been about four percent since the beginning of the year, declined in April and is currently at 3.8 percent, a year-on-year increase of one percent.

- Zemska Banka, one of the small institutions which survived last year's clean-up in the banking sector, and Velkomoravska Banka, which has been under compulsory administration since last July, will possibly have new owners soon. Although the intentions must be approved by the cabinet, Expandia a.s. is interested in Zemska Banka and 1. Silas Group in Velkomoravska Banka.

PRAVO - While Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus belittled Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy's intention to leave the cabinet at the end of the year, the chairman of the Civic Democratic Alliance, Michael Zantovsky, takes Dlouhy's statement seriously.

- The industrial production index in the first quarter of this year was 2.7 percent less than in the first quarter of 1996, according to the Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU). For March alone, the index was minus 0.1 percent. Industrial sales in March were 1.4 percent higher year-on-year, but sales dropped by 0.1 percent for the first quarter of this year.
- By the end of April this year, Trinecke Zelezarny had gross profits of 182 million crowns.
